Scoring Weights, LCI Formula & Source Governance

Benchmark Methodology, Learning Curve Index (LCI) & Disclosure Policy

How Texas Landman & Title Tech evaluates mineral title software, computes Learning Curve Index scores, verifies primary vendor citations, and maintains transparent publisher governance.

1. Six-Factor Mineral Title Composite Rubric (100 Points)

Designed explicitly from the perspective of a working Texas CPL, RPL, title examiner, or brokerage producing defensible chain-of-title and Net Mineral Acre deliverables.

Factor Weight Evaluation Criteria
End-to-End Title Production Coverage 28% Measures how much of the real mineral-title workflow the software executes directly: assignment scoping, OCR/document reading, instrument classification, chronological chain construction, ownership calculation, curative/defect flagging, and client-ready workbook output.
Ownership Math & Source-Citation Discipline 24% Evaluates whether mineral fractions and Net Mineral Acres (NMA) use exact rational/BigInt arithmetic vs. unverified LLM prose, whether every runsheet row cites Vol/Page or Instrument #, whether multi-model or human acceptance gates block unsupported claims, and whether Texas-specific rules (Duhig, Van Dyke/Clifton double fractions, pre/post-1993 intestacy) are handled.
Unit Economics & Pricing Transparency 18% Rewards publicly posted, predictable per-run or per-seat pricing, low break-even volume, zero hidden per-page OCR markups, and clear refund/credit guarantees over opaque enterprise-only sales quotes.
Ease of Use & Learning Curve Efficiency 12% Combines day-one ease of operation with our Learning Curve Index (LCI 1–100, lower = faster mastery) measuring actual hours required for a working CPL/RPL or land tech to produce client-defensible work.
Texas Courthouse, Survey & Regulatory Fit 10% Assesses support for Texas Spanish/Mexican land grants, Abstract/Survey/Block/Section legal descriptions, RRC well/lease cross-referencing, and compatibility with TexasFile, CourthouseDirect, and CountyRecords.com.
Deliverable Formatting, Auditability & Data Control 8% Covers custom Excel/Word client templates, structured folder-tree assembly, offline/local data sovereignty options, append-only audit trails, and built-in time/expense billing.

2. Learning Curve Index (LCI 1–100, Lower = Faster Mastery)

Marketing demos often make complex tools look effortless. Our LCI measures the real hours required before a landman or analyst produces client-safe deliverables without errors.

LCI Score Band Proficiency Tier Typical Time to Full Working Proficiency Operational Profile
1 – 20 Immediate Mastery 15 – 45 minutes Guided assignment intake with zero query-language syntax or template scripting. A field landman or examiner produces a complete deliverable on the first assignment.
21 – 35 Same-Day Working Proficiency 1 – 4 hours (one afternoon) Desktop workstation or structured document reader with clear human review gates; requires learning keyboard review shortcuts, folder mappings, or portal sign-ins.
36 – 55 Multi-Day Operational Ramp 1 – 3 days Multi-module cloud platforms or courthouse abstract plants requiring familiarity with county-specific book codes, tract-index search syntax, and export templates.
56 – 75 Specialist / Analyst Ramp 1 – 2 weeks Enterprise data intelligence platforms combining GIS layers, multi-county query builders, and proprietary dataset schemas.
76 – 100 Enterprise Implementation & Admin Training 3 – 8+ weeks Full E&P system-of-record suites (lease administration, DOI/deck accounting, SOX payment workflows, custom database migration) requiring dedicated land analysts and vendor onboarding.

3. Primary-Source Citation Discipline & Known Industry Data Gaps

Every third-party product profile in our benchmark records the exact public URLs inspected and verification date (2026-11-17). Where a vendor publishes conflicting numbers across its own live pages (for example, differing county counts or pricing models between a product page and a company blog), we document both figures openly rather than guessing.

As of November 2026, no independent, peer-reviewed accuracy benchmark exists across all commercial oil and gas AI title tools; vendor speed and accuracy percentages ("99%+ accuracy," "75% faster," "10× faster") are reported explicitly as vendor claims, whereas architectural facts (such as public pricing, local OCR execution, BigInt rational arithmetic, and multi-model consensus gates) are verified from product specifications and reproducible test harnesses.
